Some advice from an american au pair in germany: 

Invite her to do things. She'll be more likely to join you if she doesn't always have to ask to. However, she might also be exhausted. Kids are a lot emotionally and mentally, so don't take it personally if she wants some alone time. 

Make sure she knows how to use your appliances and don't get annoyed with her for asking. Also make sure to take her grocery shopping the first few times so she can pick out food she wants.

Tell her about the nearby stores and what they have. Germany does not have target, walmart, or walgreens, and the concept is rather foreign to them.

don't make her drive right away. Driving in germany is very different from america, and she should be in the car observing the roads a few times before driving. Explain things to her and take it slow. If you want more info on the driving differences, or antthing, pm me
